themes_detail.label: Panhandling surge in Greenwich Village
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked to 14 this week, up 331% from the 3.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, representing the sharpest acceleration in a quality-of-life issue in the district this week.
evidence: 14 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.8)
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for surveillance (Argus) cameras and public health programs
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners on Spring Street and West Broadway about increased panhandling and felt safety changes
Examine whether NYPD response protocols or social services availability have changed in the past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Curb and sidewalk infrastructure deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped 550% to 13 this week (vs. 2.0 weekly average), while root/sewer/sidewalk complaints exploded 2300% to 3 last week, signaling accelerating street-level infrastructure failure across the district.
evidence: Curb Condition: 13 complaints last week vs. 2.0 average (z-score: 8.98)
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 average (z-score: 8.69)
Community board has requested catch basin cleaning and forestry/tree maintenance for multiple budget cycles
reporting_angles: Walk the district photographing deteriorated curbs and sidewalks; identify specific blocks with complaints
Interview Department of Environmental Protection and Department of Parks about maintenance backlogs and whether this reflects systemic neglect

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendor complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 this week, up 500% from the 0.5 weekly average, marking a sudden emergence of enforcement complaints in an unregulated market segment.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0)
Suggests specific locations or vendors generating resident complaints
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods or specific streets (e.g., Washington Square Park perimeter, Spring Street) are seeing vendor clustering
Interview vendors and residents about licensing, sanitation, and noise conflicts

themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped 230% to 83 last week from a 25.1-complaint weekly baseline, indicating either widespread pothole/pavement failure or a wave of resident frustration over road quality.
evidence: 83 street condition complaints last week vs. 25.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.5)
230% spike aligns with spring thaw and winter damage patterns
Complements curb/sidewalk infrastructure spike, suggesting district-wide street degradation
reporting_angles: Map the 83 complaints to identify whether pothole damage is concentrated in specific zones (e.g., SoHo vs. Greenwich Village)
Interview Department of Sanitation about current repair priorities and timeline for addressing backlog

themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping uptick 3 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 23 three weeks ago, up 234% from a 6.9-complaint baseline, though this is the oldest spike in the dataset and should be verified for current status.
evidence: 23 illegal dumping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.89)
234% spike is statistically significant but timing is older than other spikes
Community board has requested increased sanitation trucks and enforcement
reporting_angles: Determine whether dumping complaints have continued or stabilized in the most recent week
Identify hotspot locations and interview residents about whether this remains an active nuisance
